ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in the Indian subcontinent changed by +0.287 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.204 to +0.369), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.708 °C.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in the Indian subcontinent shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.39): the estimate is +0.07 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.09 to +0.24). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in the Indian subcontinent shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.48): the estimate is −0.0020 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.0080 to +0.0037). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in the Indian subcontinent shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.93): the estimate is −0.001 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.014 to +0.012). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in the Indian subcontinent shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.95): the estimate is −0.001 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.049 to +0.045).
